GERM 109.description: Introduction to grammar and practical vocabulary necessary for fundamental communication skills. Restricted to those who have never studied German or who have placed by examination into GERM 109. Credit may be received only for one of the following GERM 109; GERM110; GERM 111 ; GERM 121 .
GERM 109.subject: GERM
GERM 109.title: Beginning German I

GERM 110.description: Introduction to grammar and practical vocabulary necessary for fundamental communication skills. Credit may be received only for one of the following: GERM 109 ; GERM 110; GERM 111 ; GERM 121 .
GERM 110.subject: GERM
GERM 110.title: Beginning German II

GERM 111.description: Intensive introduction to grammar and practical vocabulary necessary for fundamental communication skills. Admission only to highly motivated beginning students who obtain permission of the department. Credit may be received only for one of the following: GERM 109 and GERM 110 ; GERM 111; GERM 121 .
GERM 111.subject: GERM
GERM 111.title: Intensive Beginning German

GERM 121.description: Grammar and vocabulary necessary for fundamental communication skills. Assumes prior experience in German. Admission only by proficiency examination. Credit may be received for only one of the following: GERM 109 ; GERM 110 ; GERM 111 ; GERM 121.
GERM 121.subject: GERM
GERM 121.title: Elementary German

GERM 122.description: Practice and further development of essential listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills.
GERM 122.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Admission either by placement examination or successful completion of GERM 110, GERM 111, or GERM 121.
GERM 122.subject: GERM
GERM 122.title: Basic Proficiency in German

GERM 210.description: Further development of listening, reading, speaking, and writing skills; discussion of selected literary texts, and current issues; intensive review of basic grammar structures.
GERM 210.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: GERM 122, or satisfactory score on Basic Proficiency Phase II placement test.
GERM 210.subject: GERM
GERM 210.title: Intermediate German

GERM 211.description: Reading strategies, a review, and expansion of grammar structures, supplemented with materials concerning current issues.
GERM 211.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: GERM 122, or satisfactory score on Basic Proficiency Phase II placement test.
GERM 211.subject: GERM
GERM 211.title: Intermediate German

GERM 230.description: The idea of nature in Germany from the 18th century to today. Focus on scientific, philosophical, social and political entanglements that prompt radical shifts in how German thinkers view nature.
GERM 230.subject: GERM
GERM 230.title: The Idea of Nature in Germany

GERM 270.description: Survey of medieval romances and love lyrics of Germany. History and culture of the High Middle Ages in Germany, especially courtly society. The function of chivalry and courtly literature in society.
GERM 270.subject: GERM
GERM 270.title: Knights and Ladies

GERM 280.description: Survey of German cultural history from the Middle Ages to the present. Taught in English.
GERM 280.subject: GERM
GERM 280.title: German Culture and Civilization

GERM 290.description: Survey of Germanic mythological and heroic texts of the Viking Age. History and culture of Germanic tribes, especially the Vikings. The function of myth in society.
GERM 290.subject: GERM
GERM 290.title: Viking Mythology

GERM 295.description: Examination of roots and culture of environmentalism and related technological innovation in Germany. Comparison of green practices around the world to practices within Europe and U.S.
GERM 295.subject: GERM
GERM 295.title: Green Technology in Germany

GERM 310.description: Continued practice in the four skills with focus on a selected aspect of German culture and society.
GERM 310.subject: GERM
GERM 310.title: German Conversation

GERM 311.description: Continued practice in the four skills with emphasis on developing writing skills and with focus on a specific aspect of German culture.
GERM 311.subject: GERM
GERM 311.title: German Conversation and Composition

GERM 316.description: Development of advanced language and cultural skills necessary for functioning in the professional world of German-speaking countries.
GERM 316.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in GERM 210 and GERM 211.
GERM 316.subject: GERM
GERM 316.title: Advanced German for Business and Other Professions I

GERM 320.description: Literary-historical analysis and discussion of texts from German Kabarett, including comedic skits, political and social satire, parody, humorous poetry. Semester ends with a public performance in German.
GERM 320.subject: GERM
GERM 320.title: German Kabarett Production

GERM 333.description: Intensive language practice and cultural studies. May be repeated for credit by permission.
GERM 333.subject: GERM
GERM 333.title: Study of German Abroad

GERM 340.description: An introduction to the literary genres illustrated by masterpieces in German poetry, drama, and prose.
GERM 340.subject: GERM
GERM 340.title: Readings in German Literature

GERM 398.description: Taught in English. Intensive study of cultural and/or literary movements in German-speaking countries. Course content varies by title.
GERM 398.subject: GERM
GERM 398.title: Selected Topics

GERM 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
GERM 399.subject: GERM
GERM 399.title: Independent Study

GERM 401P.description: Introduction to principles of foreign language instruction and field experience planning instruction and teaching German to children in local elementary schools.
GERM 401P.subject: GERM
GERM 401P.title: Practicum in Teaching German to Young Children

GERM 410.description: Emphasis on advanced grammar structures, with continued development of all four skills (reading, writing, listening, speaking).
GERM 410.subject: GERM
GERM 410.title: Advanced German Grammar

GERM 411.description: Advanced practice in correct spoken idiomatic German with special focus on issues of the 20th century and contemporary culture.
GERM 411.subject: GERM
GERM 411.title: Advanced German Conversation

GERM 416.description: Development of advanced language and cultural skills necessary for functioning in the professional world of German-speaking countries. Preparation for standardized exams.
GERM 416.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in GERM 310 and GERM 311.
GERM 416.subject: GERM
GERM 416.title: Advanced German for Business and Other Professions II

GERM 420.description: Survey of German literature and culture from the beginnings to 1350, including Germanic mythology and heroic poetry, conversion to Christianity, courtly romance and love lyric, mystical writings, art and architecture.
GERM 420.subject: GERM
GERM 420.title: Medieval German Literature and Culture

GERM 430.description: German literature and culture of the 18th century with emphasis on the period between 1750 and Weimar Classicism. May include major works by Lessing, Goethe, and Schiller.
GERM 430.subject: GERM
GERM 430.title: The German Enlightenment and its Countercurrents

GERM 440.description: German literary, cultural, and intellectual developments from Unification to the end of WWII, including Naturalism, Expressionism, the Weimar Republic, the Third Reich, and the exile period.
GERM 440.subject: GERM
GERM 440.title: German Literature and Culture from 1800-1871

GERM 450.description: German literary, cultural, and intellectual developments from 1890 to 1945, including Expressionism, Weimar Republic, the Third Reich, and exile period.
GERM 450.subject: GERM
GERM 450.title: German Literature from 1890-1945

GERM 460.description: German literary, cultural and political developments from Post-War destruction and reconstruction, through the Cold War period of division, with examination of the reunification process.
GERM 460.subject: GERM
GERM 460.title: Post-War and Contemporary German Literature

GERM 500.description: Historical survey of the German contribution to the intellectual and cultural life of Europe. Texts and films in German.
GERM 500.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: advanced reading ability in German.
GERM 500.subject: GERM
GERM 500.title: Survey of German Culture

GERM 515.description: Structural and descriptive linguistics applied to the German language.
GERM 515.subject: GERM
GERM 515.title: Introduction to German Linguistics

GERM 516.description: Development of German in the Germanic, Old High German, Middle High German, and New High German periods. Phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, and the relationship between dialects and the standard language.
GERM 516.subject: GERM
GERM 516.title: History of the German Language

GERM 517.description: Introduction to historical Germanic linguistics including a survey of the Old Germanic languages (Old English, Old Frisian, Old Saxon, Old High German, Old Norse, Gothic); comparative phonology, morphology, and syntax, typology of modern Germanic languages and dialects; and common Germanic in its Indo-European context.
GERM 517.subject: GERM
GERM 517.title: Introduction to the Germanic Languages

GERM 518.description: Introduction to the study of variation in Modern German. Traditional German dialectology and dialect geography, language and society, multilingualism in the German-speaking countries, German in contact with other languages.
GERM 518.subject: GERM
GERM 518.title: German Sociolinguistics

GERM 580.description: Examination of recurring themes and issues or of significant periods and influential styles in German film. Course content varies and individual topics will be announced with course title.
GERM 580.subject: GERM
GERM 580.title: Topics in German Film

GERM 615.description: Intensive reading for non-majors. Graduate students fulfill their foreign-language requirement with successful completion of the course. Undergraduates may take the course as an elective only by permission of instructor. Grades S/U for graduates and undergraduates.
GERM 615.subject: GERM
GERM 615.title: Intensive Readings in German

GERM 700.description: An introduction to graduate studies that includes a survey of contemporary literary theory, an overview of the current state of the profession, and instruction in how to carry out research and write at the graduate level.
GERM 700.subject: GERM
GERM 700.title: Introduction to Graduate Studies in Languages, Literatures, and Cultures

GERM 710.description: A study of Middle High German language and literature with special emphasis on the lyric and epic poetry of the late 12th and early 13th centuries.
GERM 710.subject: GERM
GERM 710.title: Middle High German

GERM 711G.description: Reading and translation of texts in of the Old Germanic languages: Old High German 711H, Old Saxon 711S, Old Norse 711N, or Gothic 711G. May be repeated for credit with a different letter suffix from options noted above. Reading knowledge of Moderna German required.
GERM 711G.subject: GERM
GERM 711G.title: Old Germanic Languages - Gothic

GERM 711H.description: Reading and translation of texts in of the Old Germanic languages: Old High German 711H, Old Saxon 711S, Old Norse 711N, or Gothic 711G. May be repeated for credit with a different letter suffix from options noted above. Reading knowledge of Moderna German required.
GERM 711H.subject: GERM
GERM 711H.title: Old Germanic Languates - Old High German

GERM 711N.description: Reading and translation of texts in of the Old Germanic languages: Old High German 711H, Old Saxon 711S, Old Norse 711N, or Gothic 711G. May be repeated for credit with a different letter suffix from options noted above. Reading knowledge of Moderna German required.
GERM 711N.subject: GERM
GERM 711N.title: Old Germanic Languages - Old Norse

GERM 711S.description: Reading and translation of texts in of the Old Germanic languages: Old High German 711H, Old Saxon 711S, Old Norse 711N, or Gothic 711G. May be repeated for credit with a different letter suffix from options noted above. Reading knowledge of Moderna German required.
GERM 711S.subject: GERM
GERM 711S.title: Old Germanic Languages - Old Saxon

GERM 720.description: Reading and interpretation of significant literary works of the 16th and 17th centuries.
GERM 720.subject: GERM
GERM 720.title: The German Renaissance and Baroque

GERM 730.description: Reading and discussion of key literary and classical works from specific 18th-century movements, including Enlightenment, Storm and Stress, and Weimar Classicism.
GERM 730.subject: GERM
GERM 730.title: The German Enlightenment and its Counter-Currents

GERM 740.description: The development of German Romanticism, its major literary works and personalities.
GERM 740.subject: GERM
GERM 740.title: German Romanticism

GERM 750.description: German Realism, its major literary works and background.
GERM 750.subject: GERM
GERM 750.title: German Realism

GERM 760.description: Currents of German literature since Naturalism, accompanied by critical reading of characteristic works by major writers of the period.
GERM 760.subject: GERM
GERM 760.title: German Literature from 1889 to 1945

GERM 770.description: The development of German literature since World War II, through critical reading and interpretation of major representative works.
GERM 770.subject: GERM
GERM 770.title: Recent and Contemporary German Literature

GERM 776.description: Basic principles of foreign language teaching in college combined with practical demonstrations. Required of all graduate assistants. This course will not count toward the 30-hour M.A. or M.A.T degree.
GERM 776.subject: GERM
GERM 776.title: The Teaching of Foreign Languages in College

GERM 777.description: Supervised direction of foreign language teaching in college. Required of all graduate assistants who are teaching. This course will not count toward the M.A. or M.A.T. degree.
GERM 777.subject: GERM
GERM 777.title: Supervised Instruction in Teaching Foreign Languages in College
